findings.description: The user_data script exports literal AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY values. User data is readable from the instance metadata service (trivially so with IMDSv1 enabled and via SSRF) and is stored in plaintext in the EC2 API and Terraform state, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.

Ingress allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0. The attached instance sits in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch and an internet gateway route, so SSH is directly exposed to the internet for brute-force and exploitation.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised host unrestricted outbound access for exfiltration or command-and-control.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and no TLS listener or HTTPS termination exists; the Apache server installed by user_data serves traffic over unencrypted HTTP to the internet.
The EBS volume attached to the web host does not set encrypted = true (explicitly commented out), so its data is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and no KMS key is specified, so snapshot data is stored unencrypted and would be readable if snapshot sharing permissions were ever broadened.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so flow records revealing internal network topology and traffic patterns are stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is defined for the log bucket, so protection against accidental public ACLs or policies depends entirely on account-level defaults.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, leaving IMDSv1 enabled. Combined with the internet-facing web server and credentials embedded in user data, an SSRF flaw could read user data and any role credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root EBS volume is created unencrypted unless account-level default EBS encryption happens to be enabled.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, places the web host directly on the internet with no bastion, load balancer, or NAT boundary in front of its SSH and HTTP services.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true means any instance launched here receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet through the shared route table's internet gateway route.

findings.issue_category: long-lived static credentials instead of role
findings.description: The instance is given static IAM user keys in user data rather than an iam_instance_profile. Static keys cannot be rotated automatically, are not scoped by session, and remain valid if copied off the host, whereas an instance profile would issue short-lived credentials.
